title: SSC, HSC & Alim Certificate Name & Age Correction Bangladesh: Court Affidavit & Board Rules 2026

metaDescription: Errors in your SSC, HSC, or Alim certificate? Learn the complete legal procedure for candidate name, parent name, and date of birth correction with 1st Class Magistrate Affidavit and Education Board guidelines 2026.
keywords: SSC HSC certificate name correction Bangladesh
how to correct name in board certificate bangladesh
heroIntro: A mismatch in the spelling of a candidate's name, parents' names, or date of birth on SSC, HSC, or Alim certificates is one of the most frustrating legal hurdles faced by Bangladeshi students and professionals. When applying for university admission, government jobs, passports, or foreign student visas (USA, UK, Canada, Australia, Schengen), even a single discrepancy between the academic certificate and the National ID (NID) or Passport can lead to immediate visa refusal. Fortunately, under the guidelines of the Ministry of Education and Education Boards in Bangladesh, discrepancies can be legally rectified through a 1st Class Judicial Magistrate Court Affidavit and board committee proceedings. Discover the complete 2026 legal procedure, required documentation, fees, and timelines.
quickAnswer: To correct name or date of birth errors in SSC, HSC, or Alim certificates, you must first execute a formal Declaration Affidavit before a 1st Class Judicial Magistrate on a 300 BDT non-judicial stamp paper. Next, publish a public notice in a widely circulated national daily newspaper. Finally, submit an online application through the relevant Education Board e-services portal accompanied by the original affidavit, digital birth certificate, and parent NIDs.

sections.heading: 1. What Types of Certificate Discrepancies Can Be Corrected?
sections.content:
Under the regulations of the Intermediate and Secondary Education Boards (Dhaka, Chattogram, Rajshahi, Cumilla, Jashore, Barishal, Sylhet, Dinajpur, Mymensingh) and the Bangladesh Madrasah Education Board, four categories of amendments are legally permissible:

  • Candidate Name Rectification: Correction of typographical misspellings, missing middle names, or surname discrepancies.
  • Parents' Name Rectification: Aligning fathers' and mothers' names with their official Smart NID cards or Passports.
  • Date of Birth Correction: Rectifying age based on verified digital birth certificates and prior JSC/Junior Dakhil records.
  • Clerical and Gender Record Correction: Amending systemic entry errors made during exam registration.

sections.heading: 2. 1st Class Judicial Magistrate Affidavit vs. Notary Public
sections.content:
A frequent mistake made by applicants is attempting to submit a simple Notary Public affidavit. Education Boards in Bangladesh categorically reject Notary Public affidavits for name and age amendments.

Statutory Requirement: By government gazette and board circular, the affidavit must be executed before and attested by a 1st Class Judicial Magistrate (or a Metropolitan Magistrate in metropolitan zones). The candidate or guardian must physically appear before the court bench and declare the factual truth under oath on a 300 BDT non-judicial stamp paper.

sections.heading: 3. Mandatory Daily Newspaper Public Notice Guidelines
sections.content: Following court execution, a formal correction announcement must be published in a widely circulated national daily newspaper. The notice must specify the examination name (SSC/HSC/Alim), passing year, roll and registration number, institute name, the incorrect record, and the newly declared legal name. The original newspaper page must be preserved for board submission.

sections.heading: 4. Step-by-Step Online Application on Education Board Portals
sections.content:
All general and madrasah education boards now handle amendment workflows online:

  1. Log in to the official Education Board e-Service Portal.
  2. Navigate to the 'Name and Age Correction' application module.
  3. Enter exam credentials (Roll, Registration, Passing Year) to pull existing database records.
  4. Upload scanned copies of the Magistrate Affidavit, newspaper clipping, digital birth certificate, and parent NIDs.
  5. Pay government fees via Sonali Seba or mobile financial channels (bKash/Nagad).
  6. Retain the generated tracking voucher for hearing status updates.

sections.heading: 6. Strict Regulations Governing Date of Birth & Age Correction
sections.content: While clerical name errors are straightforward, age reductions post-SSC/HSC face heightened legal scrutiny. Boards do not entertain arbitrary age modifications that could affect civil service eligibility, unless verified clerical errors exist from primary school enrollment records. Drafting such affidavits demands precise legal structuring to prevent administrative rejection.

sections.heading: 7. Standard Legal Format of a Certificate Correction Affidavit
sections.content: An enforceable court affidavit must delineate the declarant's pedigree, chronological academic history, exact origin of the clerical error, and unambiguous affirmation of the legal name. Incompetent drafting can delay proceedings by months; our chambers ensure strict adherence to judicial standards.

sections.heading: 8. Attending the Board Committee Hearing & Receiving Fresh Certificates
sections.content: The Education Board convenes periodic committee meetings where candidate and guardian must attend with original documents. Upon committee approval, an administrative Order Sheet is issued. Applicants can subsequently surrender outdated certificates to receive newly minted credentials.

sections.heading: 9. MOFA Attestation & e-Apostille for Study Abroad and Immigration
sections.content: For international higher education across the USA, UK, Canada, Australia, and EU nations, fresh certificates must undergo verification by the Ministry of Education and subsequent e-Apostille authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA). Our chambers facilitate complete legalization workflows for aspiring overseas students.

faqs.q: How long does it take to correct an SSC or HSC certificate in Bangladesh?
faqs.a: Court affidavit drafting and newspaper publication require 1-2 business days. The education board committee hearing and Order Sheet issuance typically conclude within 30 to 60 working days depending on the board schedule.

faqs.q: Can a Notary Public affidavit be used for board certificate correction?
faqs.a: No. Official Education Board circulars strictly require affidavits sworn before a 1st Class Judicial Magistrate or Metropolitan Magistrate. Notary Public affidavits are routinely rejected.

faqs.q: What are the official government fees for certificate name correction?
faqs.a: Education boards charge between 800 to 1,000 BDT per certificate. Additional expenses include 300 BDT non-judicial stamp duty, court processing fees, and newspaper advertisement costs.

faqs.q: Can I correct my parents' names if they do not match their NIDs?
faqs.a: Yes. Presenting parents' official Smart NIDs along with the candidate's digital birth certificate and 1st Class Magistrate Affidavit enables smooth alignment of parental names on academic transcripts.
